cards.title: map() changes every item
cards.body: `nums.map(x => x * 2)` makes a new array where every item has been changed by the function.

hi.title: map() har item badalta hai
hi.body: `nums.map(x => x * 2)` ek naya array banata hai jismein har item function se badla gaya hai.

cards.title: Chaining
cards.body: Array methods give back arrays, so you can chain them: filter first, then map.

hi.title: Chaining
hi.body: Array methods arrays wapas dete hain, isliye unhe chain kar sakte ho: pehle filter, phir map.

cards.title: Spot the bug
cards.body: It should print `10 20 30`, but prints `1 2 3`. Which line is wrong?

bug.fix: `map` makes a new array and leaves `nums` alone, so line 2 throws its result away. Keep it: `const tens = nums.map(x => x * 10);`, then print `tens`.

hi.title: Bug dhoondo
hi.body: Isse `10 20 30` print karna chahiye, par yeh `1 2 3` print karta hai. Kaunsi line galat hai?
hi.fix: `map` naya array banata hai aur `nums` ko waisa hi chhod deta hai, isliye line 2 apna result phenk deti hai. Use rakho: `const tens = nums.map(x => x * 10);`, phir `tens` print karo.

exercise.prompt: Read whole numbers on one line and print each one squared, in the same order, separated by spaces.
exercise.promptHi: Ek line mein whole numbers padho aur har ek ka square print karo, usi order mein, spaces se alag.
exercise.starterCode:
const nums = prompt().split(" ").map(Number);
